end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from where it is grown or made until it is eaten.
Compared Shimla apples with locally sourced spinach by travel distance.
Explained that greater food miles can mean more fuel use, pollution, cost, and reduced freshness.
Mentioned refrigeration, ice packs, ventilation-friendly packaging, and increased cost.
Teach-back was not passed; compared an 80 km food journey from Farm A.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and linking longer journeys with fuel use, pollution, freshness, refrigeration, packaging, and cost. They first connected “far food” with the word “far,” then gave a fuller origin-to-eating definition later in the lesson, so that mix-up was corrected. At home, ask them to choose two foods and describe which travelled farther and one effect of that journey.
